title: Country of Origin Declared (for Imported Products)
description: Detect whether the country of origin, manufacture, or assembly is declared on the package, as required for imported products by Rule 6(1)(aa). This rule is applicability-aware: it only applies when there is evidence that the product is imported. For domestic products, this rule returns NOT_APPLICABLE and does not affect the screening score.
rule_reference: Rule 6(1)(aa), Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011 (inserted by G.S.R. 629(E), 23 June 2017)
amendment_status: Inserted by G.S.R. 629(E), 23 June 2017. Not further amended.
applicable_scope: Imported pre-packaged commodities only. Not applicable to domestically manufactured products.
conditions: Applies only when the product is identified as imported (see applicability logic)

detection_method.description: The system first determines whether the product is likely imported using importer-related keywords and label cues. If import status is established or strongly indicated, it then searches for country-of-origin declarations. If import status cannot be established, the rule returns NOT_APPLICABLE.

validation_logic.pass_criteria: When applicable (product is imported), a country-of-origin declaration is found on the label.

evaluate.action: Check for applicability: search for import-related keywords (applicability_patterns). If found, product is likely imported → rule is applicable. If not found, rule is NOT_APPLICABLE.

If applicable: search for country-of-origin declarations using origin_patterns. If a country name is found → DETECTED. If origin keyword found but no country → UNCERTAIN. If nothing found → NOT_DETECTED.

observable_evidence.description: What the software can observe: text containing 'Country of Origin', 'Made in', 'Product of', or similar origin declarations, along with a country name. For applicability, import-related keywords such as 'Imported by', 'Distributed by', or 'Importer' indicate the product may be imported.
examples: Text 'Country of Origin: China' detected — origin declaration found
Text 'Made in Japan' detected — origin declaration found
Text 'Imported by: ABC Trading Co.' detected — applicability established, but no origin text found
Text 'Manufactured by Tata Consumer Products Ltd., Mumbai' detected — no import indicators → NOT_APPLICABLE

status_values.DETECTED: The product is identified as imported, and a country-of-origin declaration was found.
status_values.NOT_DETECTED: The product is identified as imported, but no country-of-origin declaration was found.
status_values.UNCERTAIN: Import status is uncertain, or origin keyword found but country name unclear.
status_values.NOT_APPLICABLE: No evidence of import status was found. The product appears to be domestically manufactured.

cannot_conclude: Whether the declared country of origin is accurate
Whether the product truly qualifies as 'imported' based on the OCR evidence alone
Whether the country name corresponds to the country of origin vs. manufacture vs. assembly
Whether the label satisfies Rule 6(1)(aa) completely for customs/immigration purposes
notes: Rule 6(1)(aa): 'The name of the country of origin or manufacture or assembly in case of imported products shall be mentioned on the package.'
This rule is applicability-aware: missing origin on a domestic product is NOT a violation.
The system uses import-related keywords as a proxy for import status. This is a heuristic, not a legal determination.

For e-commerce: Rule 6(10A) (inserted by G.S.R. 128(E), 13 Feb 2026; substituted by G.S.R. 312(E), 27 Apr 2026, effective 1 Jul 2027) will require searchable country-of-origin filters on e-commerce platforms for imported products.
limitations: Applicability detection relies on import-related keywords in OCR text. Some imported products may not have these keywords visible in the scanned image.
Country name extraction from OCR may be imprecise due to OCR errors or unusual formatting.
The system cannot distinguish between 'country of origin', 'country of manufacture', and 'country of assembly' — all are treated as satisfying Rule 6(1)(aa).
Products with mixed origin (e.g., assembled in India from imported components) may produce ambiguous results.
